sourceNotes: Seeded from HTDM roleplay performance indicators and hospitality and tourism cluster exam data.
Terms are scoped for future vocab-card, quiz, and event-filter UI use.

terms.definition: The activities a business uses to build satisfaction, trust, and loyalty.
terms.whyItMatters: Strong customer relations support repeat business and reputation.

terms.definition: Communication that informs, persuades, and reminds customers about offerings.
terms.whyItMatters: Promotion choices must fit the audience, message, and budget.

terms.definition: Helping customers make purchase decisions through planned communication.
terms.whyItMatters: Selling vocabulary supports recommendations about staff, service, and revenue.

terms.definition: Planning, developing, marketing, and managing offerings across their life.
terms.whyItMatters: It ensures offerings meet customer needs and generate sustainable revenue.

terms.definition: Tangible products in limited supply that must be produced and purchased.
terms.whyItMatters: Distinguishing goods from services underlies every business model.

terms.definition: The process of creating, communicating, and delivering value to customers.
terms.whyItMatters: This is the umbrella concept behind many cluster and roleplay decisions.

terms.definition: The assistance and support a business provides to meet customer needs.
terms.whyItMatters: Service quality is central to satisfaction and retention.

terms.definition: The blend of advertising, publicity, sales promotion, and personal selling.
terms.whyItMatters: A mix lets competitors recommend more than one communication path.

terms.definition: The structured steps that move a customer from awareness to purchase.
terms.whyItMatters: Knowing the process helps competitors execute each stage well.

terms.definition: The stages a product passes through: introduction, growth, maturity, and decline.
terms.whyItMatters: The stage a product is in drives its marketing, pricing, and distribution.

terms.definition: The inputs — land, labor, capital, and entrepreneurship — used to produce goods and services.
terms.whyItMatters: Managing limited resources is central to operations and strategy.

terms.definition: The overall impression customers have of a business or product.
terms.whyItMatters: Image affects trust, loyalty, and perceived value.

terms.definition: A relationship of mutual understanding and trust between a business and its customers.
terms.whyItMatters: Building rapport raises trust and the odds of repeat business.

terms.definition: Paid, nonpersonal communication delivered through media to large audiences.
terms.whyItMatters: Advertising builds broad brand awareness efficiently and at scale.

terms.definition: Identifying and qualifying potential customers who may need an offering.
terms.whyItMatters: Effective prospecting builds the foundation for successful sales.

terms.definition: The full range of products and services a company offers.
terms.whyItMatters: Product-mix decisions shape positioning, resources, and revenue.

terms.definition: The relationship between how much of a good is available and how much customers want to buy.
terms.whyItMatters: It explains pricing, scarcity, inventory, and opportunity.

terms.definition: A person who buys and uses goods and services.
terms.whyItMatters: Naming the consumer keeps recommendations grounded in who actually benefits.

terms.definition: A mindset committed to meeting customer needs and providing quality help.
terms.whyItMatters: It helps employees deliver consistent, customer-focused interactions.

terms.definition: Short-term incentives like coupons, contests, and discounts that spur purchases.
terms.whyItMatters: Promotions drive quick sales, trial, and inventory clearance.

terms.definition: The opening contact and strategy used to engage a potential customer.
terms.whyItMatters: A professional approach sets the first impression that drives interest.

terms.definition: A group of related products sold under one brand or category.
terms.whyItMatters: Line decisions balance customer choice against cost and complexity.

terms.definition: The rivalry among businesses to attract the same customers.
terms.whyItMatters: Competitive pressure shapes pricing, service, product mix, and promotion.

terms.definition: Tangible products that satisfy customer needs and wants.
terms.whyItMatters: Distinguishing goods from services shapes how a business markets and delivers value.

terms.definition: The commitment a company makes about the value and experience it will deliver.
terms.whyItMatters: Knowing the promise helps employees deliver a consistent experience.

terms.definition: Direct, person-to-person communication to inform, persuade, and build relationships.
terms.whyItMatters: It enables customized pitches and problem-solving for high-value sales.

terms.definition: Asking questions to understand a customer's problems, goals, and requirements.
terms.whyItMatters: Assessing needs ensures recommendations truly solve the customer's problem.

terms.definition: Grouping related products and selling them as one package.
terms.whyItMatters: Bundling raises transaction value and perceived value.

terms.definition: The money left after a business subtracts all costs and expenses from revenue.
terms.whyItMatters: The profit motive drives the decisions competitors must justify.

terms.definition: Intangible activities that satisfy customer needs and wants.
terms.whyItMatters: Services require different quality, staffing, and marketing choices than goods.

terms.definition: The actions a business takes to fix a poor experience and restore trust.
terms.whyItMatters: Recovery answers the complaint and negative-feedback scenarios competitors face.

terms.definition: Activities that build positive relationships with the public and media.
terms.whyItMatters: PR manages image, trust, and credibility through third-party voices.

terms.definition: A product's characteristics and the value those characteristics give.
terms.whyItMatters: Competitors must separate features from benefits to sell effectively.

terms.definition: Building a company's overall reputation and identity across its offerings.
terms.whyItMatters: Strong corporate branding creates loyalty and justifies premium pricing.

terms.definition: The output produced per unit of input, such as per worker or per hour.
terms.whyItMatters: Higher productivity lowers cost and builds competitive advantage.

terms.definition: The benefit a customer believes they receive compared with the cost or effort.
terms.whyItMatters: Value helps explain why a customer chooses one offer over another.

terms.definition: Adjusting communication and approach to cultural and social differences.
terms.whyItMatters: Culturally aware service builds stronger, more diverse relationships.

terms.definition: Unpaid media coverage generated through PR, news, and referrals.
terms.whyItMatters: Publicity builds credibility through sources other than paid ads.

terms.definition: Connecting a product feature to the benefit the customer receives.
terms.whyItMatters: It turns product facts into customer value.

terms.definition: How a product is differentiated in the market and in customers' minds.
terms.whyItMatters: Clear positioning conveys unique value and targets the right segments.

terms.definition: A general, ongoing rise in prices that reduces the purchasing power of money.
terms.whyItMatters: Inflation affects demand, business costs, and pricing strategy.

terms.definition: The way customers decide what, when, where, and why to purchase.
terms.whyItMatters: Understanding buying-behavior factors lets competitors target the right message and offer.

terms.definition: A question or request from a customer seeking information or help.
terms.whyItMatters: Prompt, accurate responses signal genuine customer commitment.

terms.definition: The channels ads run on — TV, radio, print, digital, outdoor, and social.
terms.whyItMatters: Choosing the right media reaches the target audience cost-effectively.

terms.definition: A structured pitch showing how an offering meets the customer's needs.
terms.whyItMatters: A compelling presentation moves a prospect toward purchase.

terms.definition: Creating a distinct name, symbol, and image for a specific offering.
terms.whyItMatters: Product branding helps customers identify and prefer that offering.

terms.definition: The percentage of the labor force actively seeking work but unable to find it.
terms.whyItMatters: It signals economic health and shapes consumer spending and hiring.

terms.definition: The blend of product, price, place, and promotion used to reach a target market.
terms.whyItMatters: The four Ps are the standard framework for building a marketing recommendation.

terms.definition: The process of addressing and resolving customer concerns.
terms.whyItMatters: Handled well, a complaint becomes a loyalty opportunity.

terms.definition: Targeted messages sent straight to individuals by mail, email, or phone.
terms.whyItMatters: Direct marketing allows personalized, measurable, one-to-one engagement.
